title: Ben Webster learns saxophone from Lester and the elder Young
summary: In Albuquerque Ben Webster came as a poor pianist, so Lee's father taught him saxophone, practicing alongside Lester.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: the carnivals, before I get off that -- as I said before, I think my dad, I think he got Cootie in Mobile, Alabama or Birmingham, Alabama, and then in later years when we were on the way from Minnesota -- and I'm skipping some of that -- to come west, we were in Albuquerque, New Mexico, and that's the first time we met Ben Webster.

Well, Ben Webster came to my dad as a piano player, and at the time my dad needed a saxophone, and Ben couldn't play but two keys -- he could play in B flat and C on the piano, and so my dad told him he was not a piano -- he was not a pianist. Ben and some fellow from Chicago -- his name was -- he was a violin player, and they came and so my dad got him with Lester and taught Ben to play saxophone, because he needed a saxophone player.
You say he got him in with Lester, so he learned by playing along with Lester?

Yeah. Oh yes, uh huh. They used to practice together. But you see, at the time, Lester played alto and Ben was playing tenor, because, see, my sister was not going to play any more, and so she was playing -- and so she was gonna sing with the band.
